newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, good buying lifts Can dlr.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, good buying lifts Can dlr.

text.p: IMM currency futures wrapped up a lackluster session mixed, but heavy buying in the Canadian dollar pit propelled December to a contract high, traders and analysts said.

December Canadian dollars set a contract high of $0.7542 during pit trade on spill-over buying after one U.S. firm, which has been a consistently heavy buyer of Canadian dollars in the last month, bought 4,000 June contracts.
The next upside target for December Canadian dollars is at $0.7550, or 1.3280 spot, and at $0.7594, or 1.3200 spot, floor analysts said.
Marks and yen ended with slim gains, but are expected to resume declines in the near term.
"The U.S. just couldn't take dollar/mark above 1.5200 spot," a trader said. The 1.5200 level roughly corresponds to December mark's day trading low of $0.6597.
Traders and analysts attributed the firm tone in marks and yen to hedge fund profit-taking in the dollar after the U.S. currency's euphoric rally on initial U.S. election results.
Swiss franc futures remained on the defensive as the spot rate held above the 1-3/4-year settlement high of 1.2671 all day. Traders are looking for a spot rate of 1.2870 near term.
The 1.2870 level is equivalent to $0.7800 in December Swiss francs. December set a contract low of $0.7811 during Wednesday's GLOBEX session.
Several analysts noted expectations that the Swiss National Bank will soon signal to the market that it does not favor higher money market rates.
"They (the bank) have already made this clear," one analyst said. "They will move to devalue their currency and that will drag marks lower," as the currencies tend to move in tandem.
Mark futures remain range-bound, as dollar/mark appears reluctant to rise above a five-month high.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was up $0.000010 at $0.008822, marks were up $0.0003 at $0.6607, Swiss francs were down $0.0010 at $0.7859, sterling lost $0.0046 at $1.6406, Canadian dollars were up $0.0006 at a contract settlement high of $0.7539, Australian dollars rose $0.0047 at $0.7908 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000075 at $0.123125. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
